source_families: Veritasium orientation plus Axelrod cooperation literature
interpretation: The diagrams are useful as simulation, proof-status, cooperation, and workflow artifacts, but none authorizes a hard patient-outcome claim. Every multimodal transfer must preserve the simulation map, provenance, context, consent, and authority boundary.

rows.mathematical_lesson: A compact picture can guide or carry proof only when its formal rules are explicit.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: A wound photo, waveform, or chart screenshot can explain a claim, but it cannot authorize a clinical claim without the rule set that links picture features to clinical state.

rows.mathematical_lesson: Whether a pictured entity is treated as real or virtual depends on the chosen simulation.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: Latent states, imputed values, reconstructed notes, and generated captions must stay labeled as virtual until validated against the clinical target.

rows.mathematical_lesson: A visual duality can preserve a relationship while changing the representation.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: Coarse-graining or blurring may preserve some invariants while flipping others, so the runtime monitor must test the boundary after transformation.

rows.diagram_object: string Fourier transform, multiplication, and convolution
rows.mathematical_lesson: A rotation or transform can exchange operations while preserving a formal identity.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: Modality transforms such as speech-to-text, image summarization, coding, or privacy blurring need decodability and provenance checks before downstream claims inherit evidence.

rows.mathematical_lesson: A rotated or reused picture can represent a different algebraic object under a different simulation map.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: The same screenshot, plot, or body image can mean different things under different preprocessing, population, device, or clinical-context maps.

rows.mathematical_lesson: A complex protocol can be inspected pictorially only when each operation has a declared role.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: An agentic multimodal workflow may be auditable as a staged diagram, but every handoff, authority boundary, and output action needs an explicit runtime gate.

rows.diagram_object: R1 -> L1 -> R2 -> L2 -> R3 -> L3 -> R4 progression
rows.mathematical_lesson: Repeated movement between reality and language can discover new structures, but each transfer creates a new validation problem.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: A clinical note, caption, image, embedding, summary, and answer are different evidence objects; each transfer resets provenance and validation requirements.

rows.source_family: Veritasium orientation plus Axelrod cooperation literature
rows.page_or_context: Veritasium page dated 2024-01-15; Axelrod/Hamilton 1981 and Wu/Axelrod 1995
rows.diagram_object: Prisoner's Dilemma payoff matrix and repeated trust/noise dynamics
rows.mathematical_lesson: Repeated interaction can sustain cooperation, but noisy actions can cause mistaken retaliation unless the strategy distinguishes error from intent.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: Low adoption, missing data, family-consent conflict, or clinician disagreement should be audited for noise, burden, and context before the system treats it as defection or refusal.

rows.diagram_object: bulk and edge loop-equation hierarchy for Sine_beta and Airy_beta statistics
rows.mathematical_lesson: Universal local statistics are characterized by a hierarchy of approximate equations, not by visual resemblance to a reference ensemble.
rows.medical_runtime_lesson: Population, sensor, transcript, or genomic clusters that look universal should still pass the declared hierarchy of endpoint, provenance, transport, privacy, and authority checks before the LLM transports a claim.
